In fiscal 2025 (ended June 30, 2025), Microsoft changed how it reports its operating segments. In August 2024, the company announced changes to segment composition, most notably bringing the commercial components of Microsoft 365 together in the Productivity and Business Processes segment [1]. Beginning in fiscal 2025, the information provided to the chief operating decision maker reflects these new segments [1].

Effect on prior-period figures: Microsoft recast prior period segment information to conform to the new segment structure [2]. The recast had no impact on consolidated financial statements (balance sheets, income statements, or cash flow statements) [3]. The changes primarily impacted Note 8 (Goodwill), Note 12 (Unearned Revenue), and Note 18 (Segment Information) [4]. Goodwill was reallocated across impacted reporting units using a relative fair value approach [5].

Additionally, Microsoft adopted a new FASB standard on segment reporting in fiscal 2025, which resulted in incremental disclosures, most notably the disclosure of cost of revenue and operating expenses for each reportable segment [6].

The three reportable segments are: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Segment revenue for fiscal 2025 (with recast FY2024 comparisons) was: Productivity and Business Processes $120,810 million (up 13% from $106,820 million), Intelligent Cloud $106,265 million (up 21% from $87,464 million), and More Personal Computing $54,649 million (up 7% from $50,838 million). Total revenue was $281,724 million, up 15% from $245,122 million, with total operating income of $128,528 million, up 17% from $109,433 million [7].
